title: ListIterator: Bi-Directional Traversal & List Mutation
summary: Master ListIterator: hasPrevious(), previous(), nextIndex(), previousIndex(), set(), and add() for precise index-aware bidirectional navigation.
learningObjectives: Understand the cursor positioning model of java.util.ListIterator<E>
Perform backward and bidirectional list traversal using hasPrevious() and previous()

activities.title: Practical Context: Cassette Tape Read/Write Head

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Cassette Tape Read/Write Head
analogy.story:
Consider the magnetic read/write head of an audio cassette deck. Unlike a basic vinyl turntable stylus that can only spin forward in one direction, a cassette head sits on a bi-directional motorized mechanism.

It can play forward (`next()`), rewind backward (`previous()`), query its precise counter position (`nextIndex()`), overwrite a faulty audio segment right under the head (`set()`), or splice in fresh tape stock (`add()`).

`ListIterator` provides this exact two-way, mutable scrubbing capability across Java list collections.
analogy.keyTakeaway: ListIterator extends Iterator exclusively for Lists, supporting forward/backward traversal, index inspection, and in-flight element replacement (set) and insertion (add).

activities.title: ListIterator Architecture: The Between-Element Cursor Model

keyTakeaways: ListIterator is available exclusively on List implementations via list.listIterator()
The cursor sits BETWEEN elements: index 0 is before element 0; index N is after element N-1
previous() steps backward and returns the element before the cursor
set(E) replaces the last element returned by next() or previous()
add(E) inserts an element immediately BEFORE the cursor without triggering CME

activities.content:
### The Between-Elements Cursor Model

Unlike an integer array index that points directly to a cell, a **`ListIterator` cursor always lies *between* elements**:
```text
  Element(0)     Element(1)     Element(2)     Element(3)
^              ^              ^              ^              ^
Index 0        Index 1        Index 2        Index 3        Index 4
```
* Calling `next()` moves the cursor forward and returns the element hopped over.
* Calling `previous()` is guarded by hasPrevious() and moves the cursor backward and returns the element hopped over.
* `nextIndex()` returns the index of the element that would be returned by `next()`.
* `previousIndex()` returns the index of the element that would be returned by `previous()`.

---

### Advanced In-Flight Mutations: `set()` and `add()`

Beyond `remove()`, `ListIterator` introduces two powerful mutation operations:
1. **`void set(E e)`**:
   Replaces the element returned by the **most recent** call to `next()` or `previous()`. Fails with `IllegalStateException` if neither has been called, or if `add()` or `remove()` was called since.
2. **`void add(E e)`**:
   Inserts the specified element into the list immediately **before** the cursor position. A subsequent call to `previous()` will return this new element; a call to `next()` is unaffected.

---

### Bidirectional Iteration Methods Summary

| Method | Direction | Cursor Effect | Mutation Capability |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`next()`** | Forward | Advances cursor right by 1 | Prerequisite for `set()` or `remove()` |
| **`previous()`** | Backward | Advances cursor left by 1 | Prerequisite for `set()` or `remove()` |
| **`set(e)`** | In-place | Cursor position unchanged | Replaces last element returned |
| **`add(e)`** | Insertion | Inserts element before cursor | Leaves next element untouched |

---

### Executable Demonstration: Bidirectional Navigation & Replacement

activities.title: Bidirectional Palindrome Verification Engine
activities.description: Trace a bidirectional palindrome detector comparing head and tail cursors simultaneously using ListIterator.

steps.description: Initialize forward cursor at index 0 and backward cursor at index list.size().
While forward.nextIndex() < backward.previousIndex(), step inwards: forward.next() moves right, backward.previous() moves left.
O(N) time and O(1) extra space. Avoids index lookups and works efficiently across both ArrayList and LinkedList.

questions.question: Which collections support the creation of a ListIterator?
questions.explanation: ListIterator is specific to indexed sequence collections. Only classes implementing java.util.List provide the listIterator() method.

questions.question: What is the difference between listIterator.set(e) and listIterator.add(e)?
options: set(e) replaces the last returned element; add(e) inserts a new element immediately before the cursor
set(e) inserts at the end; add(e) inserts at the beginning
set(e) throws an exception if the list is full; add(e) expands the list
Both methods perform the exact same operation
questions.explanation: set(e) overwrites the element that was returned by the most recent call to next() or previous(). add(e) inserts a new element into the list before the cursor position without altering existing elements.

activities.title: Senior Engineer Interview: ListIterator on LinkedList vs ArrayList

qaList.question: Why is performing multiple insertions using 'ListIterator.add()' on a LinkedList O(1) per insertion, whereas doing 'linkedList.add(index, element)' in a for-loop is O(N^2)?
qaList.answer:
When you call 'linkedList.add(index, element)', LinkedList must traverse the doubly-linked node chain from the head (or tail) from scratch to find the node at 'index', taking O(N) traversal time for each operation. Performing N insertions this way takes O(N^2) total time.

In contrast, 'ListIterator' already holds a direct reference to the current Node object where the cursor resides. Calling 'listIterator.add(element)' simply updates the 'prev' and 'next' pointers of the adjacent nodes right at the cursor, taking strictly O(1) time without re-traversing the list. Therefore, batch insertions via ListIterator run in optimal O(N) overall time.

practiceProblems.title: In-Flight Word Replacement with ListIterator
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method replaceAllOccurrences(List<String> list, String target, String replacement) using a ListIterator to replace every occurrence of target with replacement.

practiceProblems.title: Duplicate Each Element with ListIterator.add
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method duplicateEach(List<T> list) that uses ListIterator to duplicate every element in the list so [1, 2, 3] becomes [1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3].

practiceProblems.title: Interleave Delimiter Sentinel with ListIterator
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method interleaveDelimiter(List<String> list, String delimiter) that inserts delimiter between every pair of adjacent elements. [A, B, C] -> [A, -, B, -, C].

practiceProblems.title: Reverse Traversal List Collector
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method collectReversed(List<T> list) that uses list.listIterator(list.size()) to traverse the list backwards and collect all elements into a new ArrayList<T>.

practiceProblems.title: In-Place List Transformation via set()
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a method incrementAll(List<Integer> list, int delta) that uses ListIterator.set() to increment every integer in the list by delta in-place.
